'''Delta Lake''' is an open-source [[open table format]] and storage framework
for [[data lake]]s. It adds [[ACID]] transactions, schema enforcement and
evolution, and point-in-time ("time travel") queries to data stored as
[[Apache Parquet]] files in [[cloud storage|object storage]], and it is one of
the storage layers used to build a [[data lakehouse]] architecture.<ref name="ibm">{{cite web |title=What is Delta Lake? |work=IBM |url=https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/delta-lake}}</ref>
Its central mechanism is an ordered transaction log, stored alongside the data
files, that records every change to a table as an atomic commit.<ref name="vldb2020">{{cite journal |last1=Armbrust |first1=Michael |display-authors=etal |title=Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores |journal=Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment |volume=13 |issue=12 |pages=3411–3424 |year=2020 |doi=10.14778/3415478.3415560}}</ref>

Delta Lake was developed at [[Databricks]] and released as open source in 2019.
Later that year it was contributed to the [[Linux Foundation]] under an open
governance model, and in 2022 the remaining Databricks-only features were also
released as open source.<ref name="tc2019">{{cite web |last=Lardinois |first=Frederic |title=Databricks brings its Delta Lake open source project to the Linux Foundation |work=[[TechCrunch]] |date=2019-10-15 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/15/databricks-brings-its-delta-lake-open-source-project-to-the-linux-foundation/}}</ref><ref name="iw2022">{{cite web |last=Ghoshal |first=Anirban |title=Databricks open sources its Delta Lake data lakehouse |work=[[InfoWorld]] |date=2022-06-28 |url=https://www.infoworld.com/article/2335877/databricks-open-sources-its-delta-lake-data-lake.html}}</ref>

== History ==

Delta Lake originated at [[Databricks]]. According to the Linux Foundation, the
project was launched in October 2017; it was announced publicly and released as
open source in 2019.<ref name="lfpress">{{cite press release |title=The Delta Lake Project Turns to Linux Foundation to Become the Open Standard for Data Lakes |publisher=[[Linux Foundation]] |date=2019-10-16 |url=https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/press-release/the-delta-lake-project-turns-to-linux-foundation-to-become-the-open-standard-for-data-lakes}}</ref>
On October 16, 2019, the Linux Foundation announced it would host the project
under an open governance model.<ref name="lfpress" /><ref name="tc2019" />

In June 2022, Databricks released the remaining Databricks-only Delta Lake
features as open source in Delta Lake 2.0, including performance features such as
data skipping via Z-ordering and Change Data Feed.<ref name="iw2022" /> Later
releases added a table-features mechanism for enabling individual protocol
capabilities, and the UniForm interoperability feature (2023).<ref name="tablefeatures">{{cite web |title=Delta Lake Table Features |work=delta.io |date=2023-07-27 |url=https://delta.io/blog/2023-07-27-delta-lake-table-features/}}</ref>

== Architecture ==

A Delta Lake table consists of Parquet data files together with a transaction
log, conventionally stored in a {{code|_delta_log}} directory. Each change to the
table, such as adding or removing files or changing the schema, is recorded as an
atomic commit in the log. Reading a table means reconstructing its
current state by replaying the log; because each commit is versioned, an engine
can also read an earlier version of the table, which supports time-travel queries
and rollback.<ref name="vldb2020" />

The log design lets multiple readers and writers operate on the same table while
seeing a consistent view, and it enforces the table's declared schema on writes.
The 2020 paper describing Delta Lake reported that this approach improved
performance and manageability compared with storing raw files directly, using the
log to enable optimizations such as data skipping.<ref name="vldb2020" /> The log
protocol is published as an open specification.<ref name="protocol">{{cite web |title=Delta Transaction Log Protocol (PROTOCOL.md) |work=delta-io/delta |publisher=[[Linux Foundation]] |url=https://github.com/delta-io/delta/blob/master/PROTOCOL.md}}</ref>

== Governance and ecosystem ==

Delta Lake is a project of the [[Linux Foundation]] and is licensed under the
[[Apache License]] 2.0. Its reference implementation is developed in the public
{{code|delta-io/delta}} repository, and it provides interfaces for [[Apache Spark]]
and other engines including Trino, PrestoDB, [[Apache Flink]], and Apache Hive,
as well as a separate Rust and Python implementation.<ref name="protocol" /><ref name="ibm" />

== Ecosystem fragmentation and the Delta Kernel ==

As Delta Lake added optional capabilities over time, tables could use protocol
features that a given engine did not implement. Delta uses a table-features
mechanism in which a table declares the reader and writer features it requires; a
client can read or write a table only if it supports all of the features the
table declares.<ref name="tablefeatures" /><ref name="protocol" /> Because each
engine implemented the protocol separately, support for newer features arrived
unevenly, and a table written by one tool could be unreadable by
another.<ref name="tablefeatures" />

To address this, the Delta Lake community developed the Delta Kernel, a library
that implements the protocol's semantics behind a stable [[API]], so an engine
can support Delta tables without reimplementing the specification. It is
developed in two implementations: a [[Java (programming language)|Java]] kernel
and a [[Rust (programming language)|Rust]] kernel ({{code|delta-kernel-rs}}). By
2025 several engines, including [[DuckDB]] and ClickHouse, consumed Delta tables
through the kernel rather than through a bespoke implementation.<ref name="kernel">{{cite web |title=Delta Kernel |work=delta.io |url=https://delta.io/blog/delta-kernel/}}</ref><ref name="kernelrepo">{{cite web |title=delta-io/delta-kernel-rs |publisher=[[Linux Foundation]] |url=https://github.com/delta-io/delta-kernel-rs}}</ref>
The kernel is an ongoing effort; as of 2025 its read interfaces were more mature
than its write interfaces.<ref name="kernelrepo" />

== Relation to other table formats ==

Delta Lake is one of several open table formats, alongside [[Apache Iceberg]] and
Apache Hudi. To ease interoperability, Databricks introduced UniForm in 2023,
which lets a Delta table also expose Iceberg- and Hudi-compatible metadata over a
single copy of the data.<ref name="siunif">{{cite web |title=Databricks' Delta Lake 3.0 bridges compatibility gaps with Apache Iceberg and Hudi |work=SiliconANGLE |date=2023-06-28 |url=https://siliconangle.com/2023/06/28/databricks-delta-lake-3-0-bridges-compatibility-gaps-apache-iceberg-hudi/}}</ref>
The relationship between Delta Lake and Iceberg has often been described as a
rivalry; in 2024 Databricks acquired Tabular, a company founded by Iceberg's
original creators, and said it aimed to move the two formats toward a common
standard.<ref name="cnbctabular">{{cite web |title=Databricks is buying data optimization startup Tabular |work=[[CNBC]] |date=2024-06-04 |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/04/databricks-is-buying-data-optimization-startup-tabular.html}}</ref>
